messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a p95 regression on the latest runtime build when running the replay harness against prod traces. Need to triage kernel selection + env parity.
anya: ugh, numbers? which model/profile and what GPU?
sam: model=redwood-7b-quant, profile=chat-llm-long, p50 40ms -> 42ms (fine) but p95 210ms -> 360ms. run on A100-80GB (cloud-pool-a).
bench-bot: automatic report: run_id=2026-03-10_22:14, harness=replay, p50=42ms, p95=360ms, tail_op=kernel_switch, kernel_version=auto-v2.3.1, avg_batch=6.2, kv_hit_rate=72%
kevin: did we change kernel selection heuristics in this build? I remember a recent patch to prefer sparse-friendly kernels for long sequences.
lina: yes, #3245 changed kernel selection order to prefer matmul-sparse for sequence>256 because of past gains on H100. That might be misfiring on A100.
anya: are the replay traces identical to the synthetic traffic we used for regression tests? could be input dist mismatch -> different batch/seq distribution.
sam: replay uses real-prod traces with variable seq lengths (16..1024) and bursty arrival; synthetic used fixed seq=512, steady poisson arrival. apples-to-apples was not enforced for driver & image either.
kevin: list envs pls (driver, cuda, image, kernel flags).
ops-bot: env snapshot (from run_id=2026-03-10_22:14): GPU=A100-SXM-80GB, driver=525.85.12, cuda=11.8, container_image=redwood/runtime:2026-03-10, docker_args="--gpus all", kernel_cmdline flags="nmi_watchdog=0 intel_iommu=on"
anya: compare that to the synthetic baseline run_id=2026-03-02_03:40: driver=535.86.10, cuda=12.1, image=redwood/runtime:2026-03-02, kernel_cmdline flags="nmi_watchdog=0".
kevin: aha — driver/CUDA mismatch could change kernel heuristics or library selection (cublas/cuBLASLt behavior). Also runtime image bump included libcusparse/lt updates.
lina: also note the newer image has an updated kernel selector that prefers kernel "mm_sparse_v3" when avg_seq>256. On A100 mm_sparse_v3 is slower than mm_dense_v1 due to different tile sizes. We optimized mm_sparse_v3 on H100 first.
sam: so multiple axes: (1) different input distribution (replay vs synthetic), (2) driver/CUDA differences, (3) container image with new kernel selector, (4) KV cache miss behavior.
anya: about KV cache — bench-bot reported kv_hit_rate 72% in replay; synthetic was 94%. Lower hit rate increases token work and may change kernel selection mid-request.
kevin: that could trigger more kernel switches: initial tokens choose one kernel, later tokens choose another -> extra overhead. We should capture kernel switch count per request.
lina: agreed. Proposed repro checklist:
- reproduce locally on same GPU type with the exact container image and driver (use marathon staging A100 pool).
- run both synthetic (seq=512 steady) and replay (same traces) with kernel selector in auto mode and forced mode.
- collect perf counters: kernel switch events, nvprof traces, cuBLASLt timings, context switch counts.
- dump kv cache hit/miss per request.
- run with kernel selector forced to mm_dense_v1 and mm_sparse_v3 to compare.

kevin: sample commands:
```
# run replay harness
./harness/replay_runner --trace traces/mar-01-prod.json --image redwood/runtime:2026-03-10 --cuda 11.8 \
  --driver 525.85.12 --gpus a100 --dump-kernel-switches /tmp/switches.log

# force kernel
export RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=mm_dense_v1
./harness/bench --model redwood-7b-quant --batching auto --duration 10m
```

ops-bot: reminder: when changing driver on cloud nodes, coordinate with infra team; we have an open change window tonight 02:00 UTC.
anya: What about apples-to-apples baseline? we should rebuild the synthetic baseline image with the new runtime image and run it under the same driver to validate.
sam: yes. Also consider making a small synthetic trace that mirrors replay's seq distribution (mix of 16/32/64/256/512/1024) to catch the KV cold-hit thrash.
kevin: for profiling, add these counters: kernel_switch_count, avg_kernel_latency, kv_hits_per_request, batch_size_distribution, queue_latency.
lina: I'll add a perf job in perf-suite with both replay and matched-synthetic scenarios. Will pin driver+cuda in job config.
anya: if mm_sparse_v3 is the culprit, we should roll back selector change or add HW map (prefer mm_dense on A100). But let's gather solid evidence first.
sam: action items: lina -> create perf job + reproduce (ETA 4h). kevin -> instrument kernel switch counts in runtime (PR to open now). anya -> produce matched-synthetic trace and coordinate driver parity. ops-bot -> reserve change window if driver update required.
ops-bot: noted. change-window reserved 02:00-04:00 UTC.
kevin: quick question: is this likely to affect Dedicated customers? we need to flag config if selector prefers sparse kernels on A100.
sam: potentially yes. I'll open an incident-flag ticket to evaluation team and customer-success to review high-usage hosts.
lina: I'll push initial results to the thread when done. If anyone wants quick access to the run artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/repro/2026-03-10_22-14 (kv dumps, nvprof tar).
anya: thanks — good triage plan. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks everyone. once we have kernel switch histograms we can decide rollback vs targeted HW mapping.
